catalog_quote: L'accent dynamique à Sugu est faible et léger. Le ton de la voix s'élève ordinairement un peu sur la syllabe forte. L'accent aigu est sur la pénultième, máne, dáki, ou sur la syllabe unique dans les monosyllabes, bá, va. Tout mot porte l'accent, excepté les courtes particules, articles, prépositions, conjonctions, comme a, ko, na, i, ta, ma, etc. Les suffixes attirent l'accent sur la syllabe qui les précède, quand ils sont monosyllabiques. Si pourtant plusieurs suffixes monosyllabiques se trouvent réunis, ou si le suffixe est polysyllabique, l'accent suit la règle, et se trouve à l'avant-dernière place. Dans ce cas, il semble qu'il y ait un accent secondaire sur la syllabe qui serait accentuée dans le mot principal, s'il était seul: lábu frapper, labúa frappe-le, ara weilabúgi ils se battent; tóbo flotter (en l'eau), tóbolaginía fais-le flotter. L'accent circonflexe se place sur une syllabe finale ou sur un monosyllabe, quand l'adjonction d'un suffixe ou la chute d'une consonne amène la contraction en une longue de deux voyelles semblables: donâ (pour donáa) sache-le; kô (pour kóo [kólo, à Longu]) eau; kisâ (pour kisáa [kisia, à Longu]) tarder.

new_statements.translation: The dynamic accent at Sugu is weak and light. The pitch of the voice ordinarily rises a little on the strong syllable. The acute accent is on the penultimate, máne, dáki, or on the sole syllable in monosyllables, bá, va. Every word bears the accent, except the short particles, articles, prepositions, conjunctions, such as a, ko, na, i, ta, ma, etc. Suffixes draw the accent onto the syllable preceding them when they are monosyllabic. If however several monosyllabic suffixes are combined, or if the suffix is polysyllabic, the accent follows the rule and falls in the next-to-last position.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress (weak, accompanied by a slight pitch rise) falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; monosyllables are stressed; clitic particles/articles/prepositions are unstressed. Suffixation shifts stress rightward so it stays penultimate (lábu 'strike' > labúa 'strike him'). A word-final long vowel produced by contraction of two like vowels (donâ < donáa, kô < kóo) carries the ('circumflex') accent, i.e. surface final stress in those contracted forms.
new_statements.secondary_stress: With stacked or polysyllabic suffixes 'il semble qu'il y ait un accent secondaire sur la syllabe qui serait accentuée dans le mot principal, s'il était seul': tóbo 'float' > tóbolaginía 'make it float' (secondary on the base's original stressed syllable).
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed short particles (a, ko, na, i, ta, ma); final-syllable 'accent circonflexe' on long vowels from contraction after suffixation or consonant loss (donâ for donáa 'know it'; kô for kóo 'water'; kisâ for kisáa 'delay').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, including suffixed verb forms; author notes the accent is dynamically weak with a pitch component. Describes the Sugu (Sughu) dialect as spoken around the Marist mission (author at Rua Sura), from direct observation.
new_statements.identity_note: Bouillon describes 'Sugu' = Sughu, the south-west-coast (Tangarare Catholic mission) variety; Glottolog lists 'Sughu' and 'Tangarare' as alternative names of Ghari [ghar1239] and files Bouillon 1915/16 under ghar1239; it is not separately coded among the Glottolog dialects (Gae gaee1238, Geri geri1237, Ndi ndii1241, Nginia ngin1246, Nuclear Ghari nucl1471, Tandai-Nggaria tand1254). The other two sources read (Codrington 1885, Ivens 1934) describe the Vaturanga (north-west tip) variety and are silent on stress.

Accent': dynamic accent weak; acute accent on the penultimate (mane, daki) or on the sole syllable of monosyllables; short particles unaccented; monosyllabic suffixes pull the accent onto the preceding syllable, but with stacked or polysyllabic suffixes the accent follows the penult rule with a secondary accent where the base word alone would be stressed; circumflex (long, accented) final syllable arises from contraction of two like vowels.
